title: P‐14.27: Samarium Charge Generation Assistant Layer for Improved Electron Injection in Tandem Organic Light Emitting Diodes

title: P‐14.25: Research on Optimization Methods for ALS Sensor performance of COE OLED Display
summary: The ambient light sensor (ALS) regulates device brightness by sensing the intensity of external light, which can reduce product power consumption and extend battery working time. Combined with the color temperature sensor, it can make the display present soft images, meeting the application needs of display products. This study addresses the new design demand of integrating ALS light sensor holes into color filter on encapsulation (COE) Panel for Organic light‐emitting diode (OLED) terminal products, targeted optimization design should be carried out focusing on the core requirements of overall machine transmittance, display‐off performance and field of view (FOV).

title: P‐14.11: Charge Generation Layer Multi‐stacking Strategy for High‐Efficiency Tandem Organic Light Emitting Diodes
summary: Tandem organic light emitting diodes (OLEDs) require efficient charge generation and balanced carrier transport to maintain low driving voltage and high optical performance. In this study, we present a charge generation layer (CGL) multi‐stacking strategy. The number of charge‐generation units (CGUs) is systematically increased by repeating an identical organic CGL structure. title: P‐14.17: A Low‐reflection Device Based On In‐cell Absorption Layer For Polarizer‐free OLED Panel
summary: This paper proposes a novel structural design for Organic Light‐Emitting Diode (OLED) that incorporates a selective absorption layer (SAL) within the capping layer (CPL). This design effectively absorbs ambient incident light while minimizing absorption of the light emitted by the OLED itself. Consequently, it eliminates the need for the conventional polarizer (POL) in conventional OLED displays, leading to reduced power consumption and improved bending performance. The incorporation of the SAL resulted in a significant reduction in reflectance by 43.1%, 38.4%, and 35.4% for the R, G, and B pixels, respectively.

title: P‐210: A Low‐reflection Device Based On In‐cell Absorption Layer for Polarizer‐free OLED Panel
summary: This paper proposes a novel structural design for Organic Light‐Emitting Diode (OLED) that incorporates a selective absorption layer (SAL) within the capping layer (CPL). This design effectively absorbs ambient incident light while minimizing absorption of the light emitted by the OLED itself. Consequently, it eliminates the need for the conventional polarizer (POL) in conventional OLED displays, leading to reduced power consumption and improved bending performance. The incorporation of the SAL resulted in a significant reduction in reflectance by 43.1%, 38.4%, and35.4% for the R, G, and B pixels, respectively.

summary: In this paper, we demonstrated a very competitive RGB tandem OLED based on ViP technology that showed low power consumption and long lifetime.
